i.norm:
Tests {@link TimedSemaphore#acquire()} when the semaphore is configured with {@link TimedSemaphore#NO_LIMIT}.

With no limit set, {@code acquire()} must never block, no matter how many times it is called within a single period. This test verifies that by letting a worker thread call {@code acquire()} far more times than any sensible limit and asserting (via a {@link CountDownLatch}) that every call returns.

The {@link ScheduledExecutorService} is mocked so that the periodic timer is never actually started in the background; we only verify that the semaphore schedules its monitoring task exactly once, with the configured period and time unit.
The length of the semaphore's monitored time period.
How many times the worker thread calls {@code acquire()}.

Configures the mock executor service to expect exactly one call to {@code scheduleAtFixedRate(...)} (the semaphore's internal timer start) and to return the supplied future. @param service the mock executor service @param timerTask the future the mock should return for the scheduled task
With no limit configured, calling {@code acquire()} 1000 times must never block, even though the time period never elapses (the scheduler is mocked).
The latch reaches zero only once every acquire() call has returned.
Blocks until the worker has completed all acquire() calls; if any call had blocked, this test would hang rather than complete.

A {@link TimedSemaphore} subclass used as a test double. It records how many times the monitored period ended. In this test the scheduler is mocked, so {@link #endOfPeriod()} is never actually invoked.
Counts how many times {@link #endOfPeriod()} was invoked.

A worker thread that calls {@code acquire()} on a semaphore a fixed number of times. For each of the first {@code latchCount} calls it also counts the latch down, allowing the main thread to wait for completion.
